pll1d15c9-d1e3477.summary: Asks why the Father is not said to be sent when known in time by someone, as the Son is.

pll1d15c9-d1e3482.summary: Answers that the authority of principle belongs to the one who is from none, from whom Son and Spirit are. The Father is the principle of the whole deity (Augustine). Even if he appeared through a creature, it would be absurd to say he was sent by the Son he begot or the Spirit who proceeds from him. So the one who appeared in flesh is fittingly called sent and the one who did not, sender.
claims: The Father has the authority of principle.
The Father is principle of the whole deity.
It would be absurd for the Father to be sent by the Son or Spirit.

pl-l1d15c9.summary: Asks why the Father is not said to be sent when he is known by someone in time, as the Son is. Because the Father has the authority of principle, being from no one and the principle of the whole divinity (Augustine), it would be most absurd to call him sent by the Son he begot or the Spirit who proceeds from him, even if he appeared visibly. Fittingly, the one who appeared in flesh is called sent, and the one who did not, sender.
claims: The Father is not said to be sent, even when known in time.
The Father has the authority of principle, being from none.
The Father is the principle of the whole deity.
It would be absurd for the Father to be sent by the Son or the Spirit.
